scope: Integrated B/C code before nonblocking followups

review.scope: Integrated working tree of ci/nine-pair-interop (tracked diff plus untracked new files)

initial_blockers.B0: Resolved for the compiler boundary. Compile-only build_scope in run_bounded (marmish_installed_state.py: _compile_scopes, _verify_compile_member, compile branch of _linux_scan). Escapes found by a global scan fail closed without signalling. Two empty post-cleanup scans required, source hash rechecked, pinned 1.97.1 toolchain copied with lstat checks and hash verification, scrubbed execve env. Local Linux proof is in docs/validation/installed-compiler-local.md. Native macOS/ARM64 toolchain copy is still a separate acceptance item, as that doc says.
initial_blockers.B1: Resolved. marmish_installed_ci.prepare calls prepare_dependencies (locked fetch, then offline warm build) before identities, inside the 625 s preparation reserve.
initial_blockers.B2: Resolved. run_client_pair calls _client_cleanup on any status other than received (Linux per-marker clean; Darwin recover plus cleanup_control; non-blocking profile lock). If cleanup fails the category becomes cleanup_incomplete, and run_clients stops and marks the remaining slots skipped.
initial_blockers.B3: Resolved. client_deadline = min(now+1034, server_deadline-166, overall-196). Server deadline = min(began+1800, overall-150). Lifetime itimer at deadline+1. Signals masked in finally. Arithmetic checked against the workflow step timeouts.
initial_blockers.B4: Resolved. Per-slot try/except in _reconcile_server (marmish_installed_runtime.py:619-643), then require(actual <= expected_paths). Covered by a 2-of-3 test.

nonblocking.finding: server_barrier stops waiting for peers at readiness_deadline = min(began+300, deadline-1200). That is stricter than the design's deadline-1200, so one slow peer build can fail the barrier falsely.
nonblocking.fix: Use deadline-1200 (or document began+300 as the intended bound) and add a test at that boundary.

nonblocking.finding: await_server calls stop_supervisor exactly at the live deadline. serve's own itimer fires at deadline+1, and daemon.close can take about 15 s, so the supervisor can be interrupted or SIGKILLed during close and server-result.json can be lost (fails closed as 'deadline').
nonblocking.fix: Wait until deadline + ~30 s shutdown margin before calling stop_supervisor, and keep the workflow step's 30-minute timeout above that.

nonblocking.finding: On launch timeout, _finish_child(interrupted=True) SIGKILLs the supervisor after about 6 s, which can orphan marmishd in its own session. The later cleanup scan catches this, so it fails closed.
nonblocking.fix: Optionally run stop_supervisor's INT/TERM ladder before the KILL.

nonblocking.finding: live_ci.cleanup has regressed against marmish_installed_ci.cleanup. It has no 'not-started' outcome when state was never created, pin_sha256 stays null on early failure, and it records no failure_diagnostic.
nonblocking.fix: Reuse marmish_installed_ci.cleanup's not-started and diagnostic logic, or delegate to it after stop_supervisor.

nonblocking.finding: The compile worker is launched as [python, worker, '--compile-worker'] without -I/-B, so the interpreter honours PYTHON* env and user site-packages, and writes bytecode. The env is controlled by the runner, so this is defence-in-depth only.
nonblocking.fix: Add -I -B and update run_bounded's exact-argv check (marmish_installed_state.py) to match.

nonblocking.finding: The README now links the metrics but does not state the per-metric definitions, whether teardown time is included, or the one-sample-per-cell caveat. Those exist only in METRIC_DEFINITIONS and the nine-pair phase doc.
nonblocking.fix: Add a short caveat paragraph pointing at METRIC_DEFINITIONS.

nonblocking.finding: The 'Require all three servers before commands' (server-barrier) step has no timeout-minutes. It relies on its internal deadline only.
The step timeouts sum to more than the 75-minute job timeout in the worst case. The always() cleanup still runs inside the job budget, but a job-level timeout would skip later evidence uploads.
nonblocking.fix: Document the critical path, or trim the deliver/await timeouts so their sum plus cleanup fits within 75 minutes.

nonblocking.finding: Any error reply other than hello/token, stale_challenge or the probe's not_found (including the client-tolerated input_closed and invalid_token) raises observer_operation_failed. DaemonObserver.tick (around line 407) then marks the whole observer failed, which fails all nine slots. This is not reachable in a correct run (fresh invocation, request-ID-preserving retransmit, fixture consumes stdin to EOF), but one anomaly takes down every pair.
nonblocking.fix: Optionally isolate failures per pair for non-security anomalies, and keep whole-server failure for unexpected submissions or binding conflicts.
